data.name: Harihar
data.gender_notes: Harihar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Combination of Hari (Vishnu) and Har (Shiva), representing the unity of these two supreme Hindu deities. The name Harihar carries the meaning “Hari (Vishnu) + Har (Shiva)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Harihar usually hope their child will grow to embody hari (vishnu) + har (shiva) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the union of divine powers and the attainment of spiritual enlightenment.
data.etymology: Harihar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hari (Vishnu) + Har (Shiva).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harihar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, the name Harihar signifies the union and harmony between two major deities, Vishnu and Shiva. Both these gods are revered for their unique attributes and are worshipped separately in various forms. The name Harihar reflects the belief that these two deities are actually different aspects of the same ultimate reality or God. This cultural significance is well-reflected in various Hindu texts, art, and traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: Harihar holds great spiritual significance as it denotes the unique oneness of two supreme deities, Vishnu and Shiva. This signifies the idea of different paths leading to the same destination - the ultimate reality or God. It also emphasizes the importance of unity and oneness in all aspects of life, encouraging people to overcome divisions, communalism, and sectarianism. Additionally, it reminds us that despite our differences, we all seek the same divine truth. Thus, the name Harihar serves as a powerful reminder of the essential oneness and unity of all things, inspiring us to lead lives that foster harmony and oneness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Harihar signifies the union of two aspects of God - Hari (Vishnu), the preserver, and Har (Shiva), the destroyer. This duality represents the cyclic nature of life and the inherent balance between creation and destruction.

historical_references.reference: Harihar is a combination of two Sanskrit words: Hari (meaning god Vishnu) and Har (meaning Hara, the god of destruction).

trends: Used as a title for deities
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Harihar remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Aditya Harihar, a teacher in Bali, Indonesia, shares that their name Harihar meaning "Hari (Vishnu) + Har (Shiva)" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
